# Error codes

Every API error is JSON in one shape: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "requestId", "issues"? } }`. Match on `code`; `message` is for people and may change; `requestId` is also the `X-Request-Id` header, and support can find the call by it.

| Code | Status |
|---|---|
| `bad_request` | 400 |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 |
| `identity_required` | 401 |
| `identity_signature_required` | 401 |
| `identity_signature_invalid` | 401 |
| `forbidden` | 403 |
| `origin_not_allowed` | 403 |
| `plan_limit_reached` | 403 |
| `not_found` | 404 |
| `conflict` | 409 |
| `payload_too_large` | 413 |
| `validation_failed` | 422 |
| `rate_limited` | 429 |
| `internal` | 500 |
| `unavailable` | 503 |
| `assistant_not_set_up` | 503 |

From the help article "API limits and errors" (`docs/help/developer/limits-and-errors.md`, reviewed 2026-11-07). The same text answers in the Ask tab on opem.app.

## What happens when I call the API too often?

Opem refuses the call with status `429` and the error code `rate_limited`, and the `Retry-After` header says how many seconds to wait before trying again. A refused call does nothing: nothing it sent is saved. Wait for the time `Retry-After` gives, then send the call again.

`syncDocuments()` in `@opem/node` does this for you: a call refused with `429` or `503` is tried again after its `Retry-After`, up to three times.

## What are the management API's limits?

Each secret key may make 120 calls a minute. Opem counts calls in one-minute windows, so a call over the limit gets `Retry-After: 60`. On every plan a secret key may sync knowledge documents (`PUT /api/v1/manage/knowledge/documents`, without prune). The rest of the management API, and prune, comes with the Professional and Enterprise plans; on Free and Basic those calls are refused with `403` and `plan_limit_reached`.

To stay under the limit, send documents in batches rather than one call per document (`syncDocuments()` batches them for you), and do not poll: [webhooks](receive-webhooks.md) tell your server when something happens.

## What are the limits on calls from the widget?

Calls the widget makes from your users' browsers, including requests you open from your own code, are counted three ways, each in one-minute windows:

- 600 a minute for the whole project;
- 120 a minute from one address within the project (an IPv6 /64 counts as one address);
- 60 a minute for one identified person.

A call over any of them gets `429` with `Retry-After: 60`, and the widget shows its usual failure message, such as "Your request was not sent. Try again.", so the person can send it again a moment later. The address is counted first, so one busy address cannot use up the project's allowance for everyone else.

The Ask tab also has a daily limit on answers for each person. When they reach it, the refusal's `Retry-After` runs until midnight UTC, and the widget suggests sending a request or trying again tomorrow ([What your users see in the Ask tab](../assistant/what-your-users-see-in-ask.md)).

## What does an error look like?

Every error is JSON in the same shape, whatever the endpoint:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_failed",
    "message": "Expected a string",
    "requestId": "req_01J9Z6Q4N8K2V7T3X5W1Y0M2BC",
    "issues": [{ "path": ["title"], "message": "Expected a string" }]
  }
}
```

- `code` says what went wrong and is the field to check in your code; the codes are listed below.
- `message` is English for you and your logs. It can change, so do not match on it.
- `requestId` is also sent as the `X-Request-Id` header on every response. Include it when you contact support, so we can find the call.
- `issues` appears only with `validation_failed`, with one entry for each field that broke the rules and the path to it.

## Which error codes can I get?

| Code | Status | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `bad_request` | 400 | The body is not JSON, or was sent with a content type the endpoint does not take. |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | No credential, an unknown or revoked key, or credentials for two kinds of call at once (for example a secret key and a publishable key). |
| `identity_required`, `identity_signature_required`, `identity_signature_invalid` | 401 | Widget calls only: the call needs to know who the person is, or their signed identity is missing or does not check ([Tell the widget who your users are](../widget/identify-your-users.md)). |
| `forbidden` | 403 | The credential is valid but may not do this. |
| `origin_not_allowed` | 403 | Widget calls only: the page's address is not one of the project's allowed sites. |
| `plan_limit_reached` | 403 | The project's plan does not include this, or a plan limit is used up. |
| `not_found` | 404 | No such path or record. An id that belongs to another project gets the same answer as one that never existed. |
| `conflict` | 409 | The change clashes with the record's current state. |
| `payload_too_large` | 413 | The body or file is over the size limit. |
| `validation_failed` | 422 | The body, path or query breaks the endpoint's rules; `issues` says where. A field the endpoint does not know is refused rather than ignored. |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | Over a limit; wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `internal` | 500 | Something failed on our side. |
| `unavailable` | 503 | A service Opem depends on is busy or not set up; try again later, after `Retry-After` when it is sent. |
| `assistant_not_set_up` | 503 | The assistant has no usable key or model for this project: Opem's model key is not configured on this deployment, the project's own key, provider or model is missing or cannot be read, or the test model is chosen on a production project. Calls from the widget get a general message; the Assistant page's test console, the Install tab and a coding agent's `get_install_status` say which. The widget hides its Ask tab while this is so ([Why does the widget say the assistant is not available?](../widget/install-the-widget.md#why-does-the-widget-say-the-assistant-is-not-available)). |

## Which errors should I retry?

Retry `429` and `503`, after the `Retry-After` wait when it is sent, or after a few seconds when it is not. The exception is `assistant_not_set_up`: it answers the same until the project's key is set up, so fix that instead. Retry a `500` once or twice with a pause; if it keeps failing, send us the `requestId`. Do not retry any other `4xx` unchanged: the same call will be refused the same way until you fix the request, the key or the plan.

## Where is the full API reference?

On the project's Configuration page, under API reference, with a snippet for Node.js ([Manage your projects and keys](../projects/manage-projects-and-keys.md)). The OpenAPI document, with every endpoint, its body and its responses, is at `https://support.opem.app/api/openapi.json`.
